_doc: The names rule sets share for what a part mounts by and what it does, so one piece of code can read any of them: a motor, a bearing, a driver, a screw. A set with "part" uses these names directly. An older set keeps its own names and says which is which in "interface". "checks" says what must hold between a part's figures (a head wider than its clearance hole). A field marked "list" holds a list, in ascending order; one marked "points" holds points of that many numbers each, one after another, in the order they are. A thread's older names are its vocabulary: clearance is the normal clearance hole, head and head_height the socket cap head, nut_flats and nut_height the hexagon nut. A profile (a beam's section), a slot family, a slot nut and a bought fitting for a frame are parts too: a profile names its slot family on each face, the thread its bores tap to and its material by their rule sets, and "drafts" holds every field of those parts with a starting value, in the order cad rules draft writes them. A rail is a miniature linear guide: its rail, its standard carriage in the set's rules and its long carriage as a variant, with the carriage's load and moment ratings. A workspace's joins set (part joins) holds how stiff each kind of join between beams is, written by cad measured from the joint rig; it has no file in the kit, which starts from @rulecad/frames' estimates. Read by cad rules check and cad rules draw.

type.says: what sort of motor, or of bearing

body_shape.says: the body's outline, seen from the mounting face

body_width.says: a square frame's side, a box's long side, or a pulley's overall width along its axis

body_top.says: what stands above the mounting face, beside the shaft

body_corner.says: how far each corner of a square frame is cut back

boss_diameter.says: the pilot boss round the shaft

boss_height.says: how far the boss stands proud of the mounting face

boss_offset.says: the shaft's distance from the body's centre, where it isn't central

shaft_length.says: from the mounting face to the shaft's tip

shaft_flat_across.says: across the shaft at its flat, or across two flats

shaft_flat_length.says: the flat's length, back from the tip

horn_screw.says: the thread that holds a servo's horn

mount_pattern.says: four holes on a square, or two

mount_hole_depth.says: the thread's depth in the part

mount_holes.says: the mounting holes' centres from the middle of the part's mounting face, x then y for each hole (x1, y1, x2, y2, ...), in its own frame (x along its length, y across, seen from the side away from that face): a board's or a supply's, read by a printed mount

mount_hole_reach.says: the farthest a screw may go into a tapped mounting hole, as its maker gives it (a supply's L): a mount's screw stops within it

board_thickness.says: a circuit board's thickness through its mounting holes

mount_ear_radius.says: the radius of an ear round its hole

mount_tab_length.says: a servo's tabs, end to end

cable_width.says: room for the wires, across the part

cable_reach.says: the wire housing's far side, from the body's centre

screw_clearance.says: a clearance hole for the screw

rated_voltage.says: the voltage its figures are given at

rated_current.says: amps per phase, or the most it works at

pull_in_torque.says: what a geared stepper starts against

friction_torque.says: friction in a built-in gearbox, at the output

torque_limit.says: the most its gearbox should see

no_load_speed.says: free running at the rated voltage

kv.says: a brushless motor's speed per volt

temperature_rise.says: the case above the room, at rated current

radial_load.says: the most sideways load on the shaft

bore.says: a bearing's bore: the shaft fits here

outer_diameter.says: a bearing's outside diameter: the housing fits here

width.says: a bearing's width along its axis; a thrust bearing's height; a profile's section across (x); a slot nut across its slot

chamfer.says: the corner radius of a bearing's rings, the most a shaft or housing fillet may be

static_rating.says: a bearing's basic static load rating (radial, or axial for a thrust bearing)

dynamic_rating.says: a bearing's basic dynamic load rating (radial, or axial for a thrust bearing)

radial_play.says: a radial bearing's internal clearance class: CN is normal

flange_diameter.says: a flanged bearing's flange, or a lead-screw nut's

flange_width.says: how thick a flanged bearing's or nut's flange is

shaft_washer_diameter.says: the outside of a thrust bearing's shaft washer

housing_washer_bore.says: the bore of a thrust bearing's housing washer: the shaft must clear it

actuation_force.says: the force to operate a switch

rating_mark.says: the rating marked on a switch's case

resolution.says: an encoder's resolution over a turn

air_gap_min.says: the least gap between an encoder's magnet and chip

air_gap_max.says: the most gap between an encoder's magnet and chip

magnet_field_min.says: the least field across an encoder's chip

magnet_field_max.says: the most field across an encoder's chip

magnet_thickness.says: an encoder's disc magnet, along its axis

magnet_polarity.says: how the magnet is magnetised: diametric is across the round face

supply_voltage_min.says: the least supply a board works from

supply_voltage_max.says: the most supply a board works from

pin_pitch.says: pin spacing along a header row

row_spacing.says: between a board's two header rows

pinout.says: what each pin is, in order

logic_voltage_min.says: a driver's least logic level or supply

logic_voltage_max.says: a driver's most logic level or supply

current_bare.says: a driver's continuous current per coil with no heat sink or moving air

current_cooled.says: a driver's most current per coil with cooling

current_peak.says: a driver's peak current per coil

sense_resistor.says: the resistor a driver measures coil current through

vref_formula.says: how the voltage on a driver's trimmer sets its current

vref_gain.says: the current limit per volt of Vref: A = Vref * gain (RMS for a TMC2209, the peak limit otherwise)

microsteps.says: the step divisions a driver offers

max_microsteps.says: a driver's finest division of a full step

thermal_shutdown.says: the temperature a driver's chip stops at

uart_note.says: how a driver's UART is wired

diameter.says: a lead screw's or smooth rod's outside diameter

lead.says: a lead screw's travel in one turn (or the screw a nut fits)

pitch.says: thread pitch, or a belt's or pulley's tooth pitch

thread.says: a thread as it is written: M3, 6-32 UNC, Tr8x8(P2)

pitch_diameter.says: a thread's or a pulley's pitch diameter

helix_angle.says: a lead screw's lead angle at the pitch diameter

friction_coefficient.says: the thread friction assumed for a lead screw's efficiency

efficiency_note.says: how a lead screw's efficiency and back-driving are worked out, and how far to trust them

length.says: a nut, linear bearing or coupler end to end; a slot nut along its slot

flange_offset.says: from a nut's short end to its flange

hole_circle.says: the circle a part's mounting holes sit on

material.says: what the part is made of; for a profile, the name of the material rule set it is analysed with: al6063-t5

tolerance.says: a rod's diameter tolerance, as the source gives it

hardness.says: a rod's surface hardness, as the source gives it

straightness.says: a rod's straightness, as the source gives it

style.says: what sort of coupler, and how it grips

pitch_line_offset.says: a belt's pitch line beyond the pulley's teeth, each side

stiffness.says: the tension that stretches a belt by unit strain, for its width: stretch = tension * length / stiffness

stiffness_per_width.says: a belt's stiffness per mm of its width

min_static_tension.says: a belt's least static tension per span

min_inside_idler_grooves.says: the smallest toothed idler inside a belt

min_backside_idler_diameter.says: the smallest idler on a belt's back

min_flat_idler_diameter.says: the smallest smooth idler running on a belt's teeth

teeth.says: a pulley's or idler's tooth count

tooth_diameter.says: a pulley's diameter across the teeth

belt_width.says: the belt a pulley or idler takes

thread_form.says: a fixing thread's family: ISO metric, unified inch, or a thread-forming screw for plastic

pitch_fine.says: the pitch of the thread's common fine partner, where one is common

tap_drill.says: the drill for tapping the coarse thread in metal

clearance_close.says: a clearance hole for the screw, close fit

clearance.says: a clearance hole for the screw, normal (medium) fit: the one to use unless there is a reason

clearance_loose.says: a clearance hole for the screw, loose fit

head.says: a socket head cap screw's head diameter, at most

head_height.says: a socket head cap screw's head height, at most

head_key.says: the hex key a socket head cap screw takes

button_head.says: a button head socket screw's head diameter, at most

button_head_height.says: a button head socket screw's head height, at most

button_key.says: the hex key a button head socket screw takes

countersunk_head.says: a countersunk socket screw's head diameter where the cone meets a sharp edge: a seat this wide at the surface takes the head flush

countersunk_head_height.says: a countersunk socket screw's head height, at most

countersunk_angle.says: the cone of a countersunk head, across the whole of it

countersunk_key.says: the hex key a countersunk socket screw takes

hex_head_flats.says: a hexagon head screw's width across flats: its spanner

hex_head_height.says: a hexagon head screw's head height

pan_head.says: a pan head screw's head diameter, at most

pan_head_height.says: a pan head screw's head height, at most

pan_head_drive.says: the driver a pan head screw takes: T10, PZ1

nut_flats.says: a hexagon nut's width across flats

nut_height.says: a hexagon nut's height, at most

square_nut_flats.says: a thin square nut's width across flats

square_nut_height.says: a thin square nut's height, at most

lock_nut_flats.says: a nylon-insert lock nut's width across flats

lock_nut_height.says: a nylon-insert lock nut's height, at most

set_screw_key.says: the hex key a socket set screw takes

set_screw_point.says: the diameter of a flat point set screw's end, at most

lengths.says: the lengths the socket head cap screw is sold in, shortest first (a countersunk screw's length includes its head); for a profile, the stock bars it is sold as

property_class.says: the steel property class its strength figure is for: 8.8

proof_stress.says: the stress a steel screw of that class holds with no permanent set

stainless_class.says: the stainless grade and class its second strength figure is for: A2-70

stainless_proof_stress.says: the 0.2 % proof stress of a stainless screw of that grade

insert_diameter.says: a heat-set insert's outside diameter, over its knurls

insert_hole.says: the printed hole a heat-set insert melts into, as drawn: no hole compensation

insert_depth.says: the least depth of a blind hole for a heat-set insert

insert_taper.says: the taper of a heat-set insert's hole, across the whole of it, where its maker asks for one

insert_wall.says: the least plastic round a heat-set insert's hole

pilot.says: a starting hole for the screw to form its own thread in printed plastic, as drawn, before a printer's measured figure (x1c.pilot_m3) replaces it

pilot_depth.says: the least depth of thread a screw needs in plastic

pilot_boss.says: the least outside diameter of a boss round a pilot hole

family.says: what sort of section a profile is: slotted for nuts (t-slot), slotted with faces wheels run on (v-slot), a plain bought section, an outline of your own (custom), or one printed in plastic

series.says: a slotted profile's base size: the side of one cell, which is the pitch of its slots and bores

cells_across.says: how many cells side by side across the section (x): 2 for a 40 x 20 lying flat. In a model, cells is [across, up]

cells_up.says: how many cells one above another up the section (y)

height.says: a profile's section upward (y); a slot nut from its seat under the lips to its back

corner_radius.says: the radius of a profile's outside corners

wall.says: the wall thickness of a tube, an angle or a channel

slot.says: the slot family in every face of a profile, by its rule set's name (slot-6-misumi), or closed for none; for a slot nut, the slot family it is made for

slot_top.says: the top face (+y) where it differs: a slot family, closed, or one of either per slot along +x, with commas (slot-6, closed)

slot_bottom.says: the bottom face (-y) where it differs, written as slot_top is, along +x

slot_front.says: the front face (-x) where it differs, written as slot_top is, along +y

slot_back.says: the back face (+x) where it differs, written as slot_top is, along +y

cells_absent.says: cells of the grid that are not there, as across,up pairs counted from 1 at the lower left with semicolons between: a C-beam is 4 cells by 2 with "2,2; 3,2" absent. The faces left open by them carry slots as outside faces do

chamber_width.says: the width of the closed hollow between two cells of a profile, where it is wider than the slot's cavity; 0 for a solid web between cells

chamber_length.says: how far the hollow between two cells keeps its full width, along the line joining the cells' middles; left out where it starts closing in at once

chamber_depth.says: how far the hollow between two cells reaches to each side of the line between them; left out where it is the slot's cavity depth (two cavities back to back)

bore_diameter.says: the bore through the centre of each cell of a profile, as extruded

bore_thread.says: the thread a profile's centre bore is tapped to, as its thread set writes it: M5

bore_at.says: where a profile's bores are: cells for the centre of every cell (the default), none, or their centres from the middle of the section as x,y pairs with semicolons between (-10,0; 10,0)

corner_bore_diameter.says: a hole in each corner of a profile, as extruded

corner_bore_thread.says: the thread a profile's corner holes are tapped to, as its thread set writes it

corner_bore_inset.says: a corner hole's centre from each of the two faces it sits between

corner_hollow_width.says: the side of the closed square hollow in each corner of a profile, where it has them (a lighter section)

corner_hollow_wall.says: the wall between a corner hollow and each of the two faces it sits behind

area.says: a profile's cross-sectional area of metal

inertia_x.says: a profile's second moment of area about its x axis (across), for bending up and down

inertia_y.says: a profile's second moment of area about its y axis (upward), for bending side to side

section_modulus_x.says: a profile's section modulus about its x axis: inertia_x over the distance to the furthest fibre

section_modulus_y.says: a profile's section modulus about its y axis

torsion_constant.says: a profile's torsion constant (St Venant's, written It or J on a sheet): torque = shear modulus x torsion_constant x twist per length. Far below the polar moment for a slotted section

mass_per_metre.says: a profile's mass for a metre of length

alloy.says: a profile's alloy and temper, as its sheet writes them: EN AW-6063 T66

cut_tolerance.says: how far a cut length may be over or under what was ordered, each way

cut_length_min.says: the shortest length a maker cuts a profile to

cut_length_max.says: the longest length a maker cuts a profile to

straightness_per_metre.says: how far a profile may bow from straight, for each metre of length

twist_per_metre.says: how far a profile may twist about its axis, for each metre of length

opening.says: a slot's width at its narrowest, between the lips: what a screw or a tongue passes

lip_thickness.says: a slot's lip, from the profile's face to the lip's underside at the opening: what a nut clamps against

lip_angle.says: how the underside of a slot's lip slopes away from the face, going from the opening outward: 0 where it is parallel to the face

cavity_width.says: a slot's widest width, under the lips: what a nut must be narrower than

cavity_depth.says: from the profile's face to the floor of its slot

floor_width.says: the width of the flat floor of a slot, where its walls close in below the lips; left out for straight walls

flank_angle.says: the angle of the flanks that close a slot in toward its floor, from the face's plane: 45 for the usual slot, 90 for straight walls

track_width.says: the width across a V-slot's chamfered mouth at the face: the track a V-wheel runs on

track_angle.says: the angle between the two faces of a V-slot's mouth: 90 for a wheel with a 90 degree V

groove_width.says: the width of a groove down the middle of a slot's floor, narrower than the floor (room for a screw's end under a nut); left out where the floor is plain

groove_depth.says: how far that groove goes below the slot's floor

nut_family.says: the slot family whose nuts a slot takes, by its rule set's name: its own, or the one it is made to match

nut_kind.says: what sort of slot nut: slid in from an end, dropped in and turned, rolled in on a spring, a hammer head, a bolt with a T head, or a plain square or hexagon nut

nut_entry.says: whether a slot nut goes in anywhere along the slot, or only from an open end

tongue_width.says: the width of the step on a slot nut's back that stands in the slot's opening and keeps the nut square to it; left out where it has none

tongue_height.says: how far that step stands above the nut's back, up into the opening

hold.says: the pull a slot nut takes straight out of its slot with its screw tight, as its maker rates it, or an estimate until it is tested

hold_along.says: the pull along its slot at which a slot nut slips, its screw tightened: no maker publishes it, so it is only ever measured (the joint rig's luggage scale)

tightening_torque.says: the torque a maker gives for tightening a screw into a slot nut

bolt_length.says: a T-bolt's shank under its head, as it is sold: 20 for an M6x20

fitting_kind.says: what sort of bought fitting for a frame: a corner bracket over a join, a flat joining plate, an inner connector hidden in the slots, an anchor connector in a hole drilled near a beam's end, a hinge, an end cap, or a levelling foot

screw_form.says: the head of the screws a fitting is fixed with, as the kit draws them: cap, button, countersunk, hex, set (a grub screw) or pan

screw_length.says: the length of the screws a fitting is fixed with, as they are sold

screw_count.says: how many screws one fitting is fixed with, each with its slot nut where the fitting names one

holes_a.says: where a fitting's screws pass into beam a (the beam whose end is joined), x then y for each: x from the outside of the fitting's corner along a (an anchor's or an inner connector's from a's end), y across the face from its middle

holes_b.says: where a fitting's screws pass into beam b (the beam a's end meets), x then y for each: x from the outside of the fitting's corner along b (a plate's along its bar, from its middle), y across the face from its middle

leg.says: a bracket's or a connector's leg along b, from the outside of its corner to its end

leg_a.says: a bracket's or a connector's leg along a, where it differs from the leg along b

thickness.says: a bracket's leg or a plate where the screws pass through it: the grip they clamp

plate_shape.says: a joining plate's shape: an L for a corner, a T where a meets b along its length, a cross for four beams, straight for two in line

pocket_diameter.says: the hole an anchor connector needs drilled across beam a near its end

pocket_distance.says: that hole's centre from a's end

knuckle_diameter.says: a hinge's knuckle round its pin

thread_length.says: a levelling foot's threaded stem, as it is sold

stand_height.says: a levelling foot from the floor to the top of the nut it stands on, screwed fully home: the least it holds a beam's end up

allowable_load.says: the load a maker allows on a fitting, as its sheet gives it

bending_stiffness.says: how stiffly a fitting holds a beam's end against turning across its axis, its screws tight: no maker publishes it, so an estimate until the joint rig measures it

twist_stiffness.says: how stiffly a fitting holds a beam's end against twisting about its own axis: an estimate until the joint rig measures it

cost.says: the price of one, as its seller lists it on the date checked, in the unit of its currency (EUR, GBP, USD), or per kilogram for a printing plastic (EUR/kg): the rule says whether tax is in it

rail_width.says: a guide rail's width across (WR on a maker's drawing)

rail_height.says: a guide rail's height from the face it is screwed to (HR)

rail_hole_pitch.says: the distance between a guide rail's mounting holes along it (P)

rail_hole_end.says: a guide rail's standard distance from its end to the centre of its last hole (E)

rail_hole_diameter.says: a guide rail's mounting hole, through it under the counterbore (d)

rail_counterbore_diameter.says: the counterbore for a rail screw's head (D)

rail_counterbore_depth.says: how deep a rail's counterbore is from its top (h)

rail_thread.says: the thread of the screws that hold a guide rail down: M3

rail_screw_length.says: the length of the screw its maker lists for a rail's holes

rail_mass.says: a guide rail's mass per metre

rail_length_max.says: the longest rail its maker sells in one piece

rail_parallelism.says: how far a carriage's running faces may stray from parallel to the rail's base: for each step, the rail's length up to which it holds, then the tolerance

carriage_length.says: a guide carriage's length along its rail, end seals included (L)

carriage_length_max.says: a guide carriage's greatest length along its rail with its seal lips and screws (L max): its travel is counted from it

carriage_body_length.says: a guide carriage's steel body along its rail, without its end caps (L1)

carriage_width.says: a guide carriage's width across its rail (W)

carriage_height.says: the height of a guide carriage's top face over the face its rail is screwed to (H)

carriage_clearance.says: the gap under a guide carriage, over the face its rail is screwed to (H1)

carriage_hole_x.says: the distance between a guide carriage's tapped holes along its rail (C)

carriage_hole_y.says: the distance between a guide carriage's tapped holes across its rail (B)

carriage_thread.says: the thread of a guide carriage's tapped holes: M3

carriage_thread_depth.says: how deep a guide carriage's tapped holes go

carriage_play.says: the most a guide carriage moves across its rail with no load, at the preload class it is sold in

carriage_stiffness.says: a guide carriage's radial stiffness on its rail, at the preload class it is sold in

moment_roll.says: a guide carriage's static moment rating about its rail's axis (MR)

moment_pitch.says: a guide carriage's static moment rating about the axis across its rail, tipping it end over end (MP)

moment_yaw.says: a guide carriage's static moment rating about the axis out of its rail's face, turning it across the rail (MY)

wheel_diameter.says: a V-wheel's outside diameter, at the flat of its rim

wheel_width.says: a V-wheel's width along its axle

wheel_flat.says: the width of the flat at the tip of a V-wheel's rim, between its two flanks

wheel_angle.says: the angle between a V-wheel's two flanks: 90 for a wheel that runs in a 90 degree V track

wheel_bearing.says: the bearing set a V-wheel runs on: bearing-625

wheel_bearings.says: how many of its bearing a V-wheel takes, side by side

wheel_seat_depth.says: how deep each bearing's seat is from a V-wheel's face

wheel_lip.says: the width of the lip inside a V-wheel between its two bearings

wheel_material.says: what a V-wheel is moulded from: delrin, polycarbonate

wheel_modulus.says: the tensile modulus of a V-wheel's plastic, for its contact on the track

wheel_poisson.says: Poisson's ratio of a V-wheel's plastic

wheel_contact_stress.says: the contact pressure a V-wheel's plastic is held to on its track: past it the rim flattens

wheel_thread.says: the thread of the screw a V-wheel turns on: M5

wheel_eccentric.says: the eccentric spacer set made for a V-wheel: eccentric-6-openbuilds

wheel_plate_across.says: how far apart its maker's plate puts two V-wheels' axles across a 20 mm beam, the eccentric turned to its middle

wheel_plate_hole.says: the hole in its maker's plate for a fixed V-wheel's screw

spacer_diameter.says: the outside diameter of the plain spacer under a fixed wheel

spacer_bore.says: the bore of the plain spacer under a fixed wheel

spacer_lengths.says: the lengths the plain spacer is sold in

eccentric_offset.says: how far an eccentric spacer's bore stands off the axis of its rim: turning it moves the wheel twice this from end to end

eccentric_height.says: an eccentric spacer's height between the plate and the wheel (its cam height)

eccentric_rim_diameter.says: the diameter of the round rim under an eccentric spacer that turns in the plate's hole

eccentric_rim_height.says: how far an eccentric spacer's rim reaches into the plate's hole

eccentric_hole.says: the hole its maker's plate has for an eccentric spacer's rim

eccentric_bore.says: the bore through an eccentric spacer, for the wheel's screw

eccentric_hex.says: across the flats of an eccentric spacer's hex, the spanner that turns it

thread.says: a tap drill is under the thread, and the clearance holes over it in order: close, normal, loose
a tap drill is about the major diameter less the pitch
a fine pitch is finer than the coarse one
a pilot in plastic is wider than a tap drill and tighter than the closest clearance hole
a pilot is close to the thread it is formed by (drawn for printing, it can pass a small thread's own diameter)
a pilot is wider than the root of the thread formed in it
a thread's root is inside its crest
a key fits inside its head
a cap head is wider than the loosest clearance hole, or it pulls through
a key fits inside its head
a button head is wider than the loosest clearance hole
a key fits inside its head
a countersunk head is wider than the loosest clearance hole
a hexagon head is wider than the loosest clearance hole
a pan head is wider than the loosest clearance hole
a nut is wider than its thread
a nut is wider than its thread
a lock nut is taller than a plain one, by its nylon ring
a washer's hole passes the thread, and its rim stands outside it
a washer covers the loosest clearance hole
a set screw's key fits inside its thread
an insert's hole is wider than its thread and narrower than its knurls, which the plastic flows round
a blind hole is deeper than its insert
the stainless figure is the lower of the two

profile.says: a bore is inside its cell
a corner hole is inside its corner
a corner hollow is inside its corner
the shortest cut is shorter than the longest

slot.says: a slot is wider under its lips than between them, or it holds no nut
a slot's floor is below its lips
a slot closes in toward its floor (leave floor_width out for straight walls)
a V-slot's mouth is wider at the face than between the lips

slot_nut.says: a slot nut's tongue is narrower than the nut it stands on
